title: Best CRE Underwriting Software in 2026
summary: Seven CRE underwriting software platforms compared for commercial real estate loan underwriting: rent rolls, NOI, DSCR, credit memos and AI, and who each fits.
body_markdown:
Quick answer


Kita is the best CRE underwriting software in 2026. It collects the borrower’s documents, reads the rent roll, T-12, appraisal, Phase I report and sponsor financials, works out net operating income, debt service coverage and debt yield with repeatable stress scenarios, applies your credit policy as rules-based decisioning, drafts a credit memo with every figure cited to its source and monitors the loan after close, all in one platform and on every loan type. Aloan, built for community banks and credit unions, LenderBox and Blooma are other lender tools, Clik.ai builds Excel models from rent rolls and T-12s, and ARGUS Enterprise and Leni serve owners and investors valuing property. Kita is our product.


Key takeaways


Kita covers the whole CRE loan: testing the file, drafting the memo, decisioning against your policy and monitoring the portfolio. The other six do three different jobs: testing a loan file and drafting the memo (Aloan for community banks and credit unions, LenderBox), screening deals and monitoring a portfolio (Blooma), and modeling property for owners and investors (ARGUS Enterprise, Leni). Clik.ai builds the Excel model in between.


Five of the seven link their figures back to a source document: Kita, Aloan, LenderBox, Clik.ai and Leni. In Kita every figure in the memo cites its source line. If an examiner asks how a DSCR was built, that trail is the feature to test.


None of the seven publishes a price on the pages we checked. Aloan and LenderBox describe usage-based pricing, so ask for a quote at your own deal volume.


**Best for underwriting the whole lender file:** Kita, which collects the documents from the borrower, checks them, builds the spread for the property and the sponsor, applies your credit policy, drafts a cited memo and monitors the portfolio after close.


Suppose a bank is asked to lend $4 million against an office building. The owner hands over a rent roll, which lists every tenant and the rent each one pays, and says the building is nearly full. Whether the bank is repaid depends on whether that rent keeps arriving, and on whether the owner, who may hold other buildings and other debts, can cover a gap. Underwriting is the work of testing both claims before the money goes out.


Commercial real estate (CRE) underwriting software takes that work off the analyst’s desk. It reads the rent roll and operating statements, works out net operating income (what the property earns after the cost of running it), and divides that by the year’s loan payments to get the debt service coverage ratio, or DSCR. A DSCR of 1.25 means the property earns a quarter more than the loan costs.\[1\] Many tools also draft the credit memo.


The tools that rank for this search do two different jobs. Lender tools test whether a loan will be repaid, against the lender’s own credit policy. Owner and investor tools value a property and model what to pay for it. Kita is built for lenders and also brings comparables and valuation analysis into the credit file.

01


## Kita


Best overall: one platform for the whole CRE loan, from rent roll and sponsor to cited memo, decision and portfolio monitoring


Kita is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform with a check in every column of the scorecard, covering the whole CRE loan from intake to portfolio monitoring. On a commercial real estate file it collects the documents from the borrower, reads the rent roll, T-12 and sponsor financials, computes NOI and debt service coverage from the spread, applies the lender’s credit policy as rules-based decisioning and drafts a credit memo with every figure cited to its source. After close it monitors the portfolio. The lender’s credit team keeps final sign-off.


-


**AI Credit Officer.** Asks the borrower for the documents your CRE policy requires, by SMS, email and the borrower portal, checks each upload as it lands and follows up until the file is complete.


-


**Kita Capture.** Reads rent rolls, T-12s, operating statements, leases, appraisals, environmental reports and tax returns in any format, including scans, flags tampering and forgery patterns, and catches contradictions across the file, such as income on one document that another does not support.


-


**Rent rolls, NOI and sponsors.** Standardizes the rent roll in whatever format it arrives, flags missing lease expirations, tenant concentration and rollover, separates recurring from nonrecurring items in net operating income with a source citation on every line, and calculates DSCR and debt yield from one documented baseline so stress scenarios can be repeated. It spreads sponsor and guarantor tax returns, tracing K-1s across related entities, and combines them across the sponsor’s other properties and debts.


-


**AI Underwriter and decisioning.** Builds a normalized period-over-period spread, computes debt service coverage, margin and trend in one pass, reads risks the ratios miss such as concentration, and applies your encoded credit policy, including DSCR, LTV and concentration limits, as rules-based decisioning that approves, declines or refers each file. It drafts the memo with every figure cited to its source line.


-


**Appraisals, valuation and portfolio monitoring.** Kita reads the full appraisal and Phase I environmental report and pulls the key sections into the file with page-level citations, adds market comparables and valuation analysis to each deal, and after close carries the loan through closing and servicing and monitors the portfolio.


-


**Your stack or Kita’s.** Kita is API-first and integrates with any external system: any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, credit engine or custom workflow. Or it runs the whole process in Intelligent LOS. It works on every loan type, on CRE books and mixed ones: Kita is in production on SBA, working capital and equipment finance files too. Kita is SOC 2 Type II compliant and ISO 27001 certified.


Best for:


Banks, credit unions and CRE lenders that want one system to collect the file, check it, spread the property and sponsor, decide against their own policy, draft the memo and monitor the loan after close, on a CRE book or a mixed one.


02


## Aloan


Best for community banks that want cited CRE analysis beside their current LOS


Aloan describes itself as the AI-native commercial loan origination system (LOS) for community banks and credit unions. For commercial real estate it standardizes rent rolls and operating statements, spreads sponsor and guarantor returns, and assembles a source-cited package for the underwriter. It runs as the lender’s LOS or alongside the one it already has.\[5,6\]


-


**Rent rolls and NOI.** Aloan standardizes a borrower’s rent roll in whatever format it arrives, flags missing lease expirations, tenant concentration and rollover, and separates recurring from nonrecurring items in net operating income with a source citation on every line.\[5\]


-


**Stress tests and sponsors.** It calculates DSCR and debt yield from one documented baseline so stress scenarios can be repeated, and it spreads sponsor and guarantor tax returns, tracing K-1s across related entities.\[5\]


-


**Appraisals and environmental reports.** Aloan reads the full appraisal and Phase I environmental report and pulls the key sections into the file with page-level citations.\[5\]


-


**What it leaves out.** Aloan says it does not produce closing documents, book or fund the loan to the core, or make the credit decision. It reports that most lenders go live in 2 to 4 weeks and 77% less time per file on a standard community-bank commercial file, from 40+ hours to about 9. Pricing is usage-based and quoted per institution.\[6,7\]


Best for:


Community and regional banks and credit unions that want CRE spreading, sponsor analysis and a cited memo, and will keep closing and booking in another system.


03


## LenderBox


Best for banks and debt funds that want policy checks and market data on every CRE deal


LenderBox calls itself an AI lending intelligence platform for commercial real estate, built for community and regional banks, credit unions and CRE private credit teams. It says it reads the loan file, checks the deal against the lender’s credit policy and drafts the credit memo, and that it compresses 25 or more analyst hours per deal to under one hour.\[8\]


-


**Page-cited extraction.** It reads rent rolls, T-12 operating statements, appraisals, leases, sponsor financials and environmental reports, with a page-level citation on every extracted figure.\[8\]


-


**Policy checks.** LenderBox ingests the institution’s credit policy and flags LTV limits, DSCR thresholds, concentration caps and geographic restrictions before a deal reaches committee, citing both the document figure and the policy clause.\[8,9\]


-


**Market and portfolio tools.** It adds cap rates, comparable sales and submarket analytics to each deal, plus maturity tracking and concentration monitoring across the portfolio.\[8\]


-


**Fit and price.** LenderBox describes itself as an intelligence layer that works alongside the LOS, and names nCino, Salesforce and Abrigo. It says most institutions reach productive use in three to four weeks. Pricing has three parts: a one-time data activation, a monthly platform fee credited toward usage, and a flat per-deal rate.\[8,9,10\]


Best for:


Banks and CRE debt funds that run many deals a month, want market comparables and concentration tracking in the same tool, and prefer pricing that follows deal volume. Origination stays in your LOS.


04


## Blooma


Best for CRE lenders that want deal screening and portfolio monitoring beside their LOS


Blooma is an AI platform built for commercial real estate lenders, from small teams to large institutions. It says it is not a loan origination system, CRM or data provider but an insights engine that sits on top of the tools a lender already uses, and it offers Blooma Pro for smaller teams and Blooma Enterprise for larger institutions.\[11,12\]


-


**Deal screening.** Origination Intelligence gathers borrower documents, integrates key financial data and identifies whether a deal fits the institution’s criteria, combining borrower profiles, property performance and live market trends.\[12\]


-


**Document parsing.** Blooma says it parses offering memorandums, rent rolls, operating statements, construction budgets, personal financial statements, schedules of real estate owned and tax returns.\[13\]


-


**Valuation and sensitivities.** Its lending page says Blooma calculates six valuations per deal, shows up to 100 comparable properties, and lets users change revenue, expenses, cap rate, vacancy and interest rate to see the effect on LTV, DSCR and debt yield.\[13\]


-


**Portfolio monitoring.** Portfolio Intelligence adds proactive alerts and continuous monitoring after origination. Blooma’s home page carries testimonials from C3Bank, SunWest Bank and ABP Capital.\[11\]


Best for:


CRE lenders that already run an LOS and want screening, valuation and portfolio monitoring in one dashboard. The pages we checked do not describe credit memo drafting or a source citation on each figure.


05


## Clik.ai


Best for lenders and brokers that want rent rolls and T-12s turned into a finished Excel model


Clik.ai’s AutoUW product turns rent rolls, T-12s and operating statements into cash flow, loan sizing and a lender-ready Excel underwriting model. The company serves CRE lenders, brokers, investors and servicers, and also sells services such as agency workbook support, lease abstraction and loan onboarding.\[14,15\]


-


**Extraction to model.** It reads PDF, scanned and Excel files, normalizes income and expenses, maps charge codes and calculates NOI, DSCR and loan sizing, then delivers Excel models in pre-built or custom lender templates through an Excel add-in, API or CRM integration.\[15,16\]


-


**Review in the loop.** A side-by-side viewer lets staff check extracted data against the source document, and Clik.ai analysts can review complex deals and work live with a team to complete Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac workbooks.\[15,16,14\]


-


**Vendor-reported figures.** Clik.ai reports 99% extraction accuracy and about 70% less manual underwriting effort. Its own pages are not consistent: the AutoUW page says 100% accurate where the CRE page says 99%.\[15,16\]


-


**What the pages do not describe.** The pages we checked describe an underwriting model, not a credit memo checked against the lender’s policy, and they do not mention sponsor or guarantor analysis.\[15,14\]


Best for:


Lenders, brokers and servicers with a house Excel template that want extraction and a first-pass model done for them, with analyst help on agency workbooks.


06


## ARGUS Enterprise


Best for owners and investors valuing property and forecasting cash flow


ARGUS Enterprise, from Altus Group, is commercial property valuation and cash flow forecasting software, now part of the ARGUS Intelligence Platform. Altus names real estate investors, asset managers, portfolio managers, research leaders and valuation professionals as its users. The page does not mention underwriting or lenders.\[17\]


-


**Lease-by-lease cash flow.** It models income lease by lease for every lease type, with market leasing assumptions for new, vacant and renewing space.\[17\]


-


**Valuation and debt.** It supports discounted cash flow and traditional capitalization methods, with detailed discount rate, terminal cap rate and growth assumptions, and debt modeling for unleveraged and leveraged returns.\[17\]


-


**Scenarios and reports.** Users run what-if, sensitivity and risk analyses across assets and portfolios and export more than 40 standard reports.\[17\]


-


**Track record and price.** Altus says it has developed ARGUS software for more than 30 years and that it is used in more than 100 countries. Pricing is tiered and quoted through sales.\[17\]


Best for:


Investors, asset managers and valuation teams that need transparent lease-level cash flow and value. For a credit file with policy checks and a memo, pair it with a lender platform.


07


## Leni


Best for investment teams that want underwriting models and committee memos for their own deals


Leni helps real estate businesses run with AI, built around a company’s own systems, documents and expertise. Its financial modeling and underwriting work takes an offering memorandum, rent roll and T-12 to an editable model with base and downside cases and an investment committee memo. Leni’s own guide describes its users as asset managers, acquisitions professionals and portfolio operators.\[18,20\]


-


**Deal underwriting.** Leni maps the T-12 into the team’s model, runs base and downside cases covering debt, rent growth and exit, and lists open diligence questions with sources.\[19\]


-


**Done for you or built in-house.** Leni says its specialists prepare the inputs, sensitivities and open questions, and that the customer’s team makes the final decision. It also offers asset management, finance and accounting, and fund administration support.\[19,18\]


-


**Linked to source.** Leni says its outputs are linked to source documents.\[18\]


-


**What the pages do not describe.** The pages we checked do not describe underwriting a loan against a lender’s credit policy, sponsor or guarantor analysis, or a credit memo.\[19,20\]


Best for:


Owners, sponsors and acquisition teams that want models, committee memos and portfolio reporting for their own deals, with specialist support if they want it.


## How to choose CRE underwriting software


Six questions separate these products more than any feature list.


-


**Whose underwriting is it?** A lender decides whether to lend against its own policy. An investor decides what to pay. Kita is built for lenders, as are Aloan, LenderBox and Blooma, while ARGUS Enterprise and Leni describe investor users.\[1,5,8,11,17,20\] Clik.ai says it serves both.\[15\]


-


**Does it test the sponsor as well as the property?** A CRE file rests on the property’s income and on the person behind it, so the sponsor’s liquidity and other debts matter when the income falls short.\[1\] Ask whether the tool reads sponsor and guarantor returns and combines them across the sponsor’s other properties. Kita does, tracing K-1s across related entities, and Aloan states that it does.\[1,5\]


-


**Can you trace every figure?** Every figure in Kita’s memo cites its source line. Aloan, LenderBox and Clik.ai each say figures trace back to the source, and Leni says its outputs are linked to source.\[1,5,8,15,18\] Ask to click from a DSCR to the page it came from, and whether an analyst’s override is recorded.


-


**Does it enforce your policy, or a generic one?** The Federal Reserve’s CRE guidance says it does not set one concentration limit for every institution.\[21\] Each lender sets its own limits, so the tool should test your DSCR, LTV and concentration limits. Kita applies your policy as rules-based decisioning, approving, declining or referring each file, and Aloan and LenderBox say they check files against the lender’s credit policy.\[1,6,8\]


-


**Does it replace your LOS or run beside it?** Kita can do either: it is API-first and integrates with any external system, including any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, or runs as the LOS in Intelligent LOS. Aloan can also do either. LenderBox and Blooma say they work alongside an existing LOS, and Clik.ai delivers through an Excel add-in, API or CRM integration.\[2,6,9,11,15\]


-


**What will it cost, and does it work on your files?** Aloan describes usage-based pricing and LenderBox a flat per-deal rate plus a platform fee, so ask each for a quote at your deal volume.\[7,10\] Then run three closed CRE files through each shortlisted tool and compare the NOI, DSCR and memo with your analysts’ work.


Our recommendation for lenders is Kita: it answers yes to each of these questions and covers the whole CRE loan, from collecting the file to the cited memo, policy decisioning and portfolio monitoring, in one platform. If you only need part of the job, Aloan offers cited analysis of the file for community banks and credit unions, LenderBox adds market data to the file, Blooma screens a pipeline and watches the portfolio, and Clik.ai fills a house Excel template. An owner or investor valuing property can look at ARGUS Enterprise or Leni.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best CRE underwriting software?


Kita is the best CRE underwriting software for lenders. It collects the borrower’s documents, reads the rent roll, T-12, appraisal, Phase I report and sponsor financials, works out NOI, DSCR and debt yield with repeatable stress scenarios, applies your credit policy as rules-based decisioning, drafts a memo with every figure cited to its source and monitors the loan after close, in one platform. Aloan, built for community banks and credit unions, LenderBox and Blooma are other lender tools, Clik.ai turns rent rolls and T-12s into an Excel model, and ARGUS Enterprise and Leni serve owners and investors valuing a property. Run one of your closed CRE files through Kita to see the result.


### What is commercial real estate underwriting software?


It is software that does the analytical work on a commercial real estate file. It reads the rent roll, operating statements and sponsor financials, works out net operating income and debt service coverage, and records the analysis. Lender-side tools also check the file against the credit policy and draft the memo, while investor-side tools build valuation models.


### What is the best AI underwriting software for commercial real estate loans?


Kita is the best AI underwriting software for commercial real estate loans. It collects the documents from the borrower, checks them for fraud, standardizes the rent roll, reads the appraisal and Phase I report, builds the spread for the property and the sponsor with K-1s traced across related entities, stress-tests DSCR and debt yield, applies the lender’s credit policy as rules-based decisioning and drafts a cited memo, with the lender’s credit team keeping final sign-off. Aloan, built for community banks and credit unions, and LenderBox also read the loan file and draft a memo, and Blooma focuses on screening and monitoring.


### How do you calculate DSCR on a commercial property?


Divide the property’s net operating income by its annual debt service. A property with $150,000 of net operating income and $120,000 of annual loan payments has a DSCR of 1.25, so its income covers the debt 1.25 times. Each lender sets its own minimum in its credit policy, and a good tool such as Kita tests your limit rather than a generic one.


### Do we have to replace our loan origination system to use CRE underwriting software?


No. Kita is API-first and integrates with any external system, including any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool or credit engine, and lenders that want one system for the whole loan can run it end to end in Kita’s Intelligent LOS. Aloan, LenderBox and Blooma each say they work alongside an existing loan origination system, and Aloan can also act as the LOS.


### What is Kita and how does it underwrite commercial real estate loans?


Kita is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform. On a commercial real estate loan its AI Credit Officer collects the documents from the borrower, Kita Capture reads and fraud-checks them, including the rent roll, T-12 and sponsor financials, and the AI Underwriter builds the spread, applies the lender’s credit policy as rules-based decisioning and drafts a memo with every figure cited to its source. Kita then monitors the loan after close. The lender’s credit team keeps final sign-off.
